name: F2a_tangent_line_above_circle
sw_rationale: Family 2 (Tangent sign). A circle r=10 with center near (0,12) and a horizontal line that is initially ABOVE the circle touching from above. The tangent constraint (dist from center to line = radius) has two solutions: line at y=+10 (above) or y=-10 (below). SolidWorks keeps whichever side the geometry was drawn on. Here the line starts at y=12 (above center), so the solver must find line touching the TOPMOST point: center.y - r = line.y means center drifts to y=10+r=10+10=20, or with center freed: line stays near y~12, center settles at y=22. We pin the line horizontal at y=15 (unfixed y, starting above the circle) and fix the circle center x, free the center y. Expected: circle center.y = line.y + r. Confidence HIGH on side selection.

expect._coord_notes: Line is at y=15, circle center at (0,12), r=5. Distance from center to line = |15-12|=3, but r=5: not satisfied. With everything fixed + tangent this is over-defined / conflicts. The fixture as written is intentionally conflicted to test what the solver reports. The interesting SW behavior: if center.y were free, it would move to y=15-5=10 or y=15+5=20. Since center starts BELOW the line (12<15), SW picks center.y=10 (below line, touching from below - center below line). REVISED: let center y be free by removing fix on center, add fix only on center.x.
expect._NOTE: This fixture over-constrains (all fixed + tangent). See F2b for the correct branch-selection fixture.
